Hi @thdxr and @rekram1-node, I think the regression is in `bootstrapDirectory` in `packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts`, introduced in #22756 (v1.4.7). The `queryFn` is correct, only the **TanStack Query key is wrong**:

```ts
// packages/app/src/context/global-sync/bootstrap.ts:349-370 (current)
const rev = (providerRev.get(input.directory) ?? 0) + 1
providerRev.set(input.directory, rev)
void input.queryClient.ensureQueryData({
  ...loadSessionsQuery(input.directory),   // ← should be loadProvidersQuery
  queryFn: () =>
    retry(() => input.sdk.provider.list())
      .then((x) => {
        if (providerRev.get(input.directory) !== rev) return
        input.setStore("provider", normalizeProviderList(x.data!))
        input.setStore("provider_ready", true)
      })
      ...
})
```

- `loadSessionsQuery(dir)` → key `[dir, "loadSessions"]`
- `loadProvidersQuery(dir)` → key `[dir, "providers"]`

By the time this runs, sessions are already cached, so `ensureQueryData` short-circuits and the provider `queryFn` is never invoked. The per-directory provider list never refreshes and `provider_ready` stays `false`.

### Why your Bedrock setup shows zero providers

`useProviders` falls back to `globalSync.data.provider` when `provider_ready` is false — but the **global** SDK does not see your project's `opencode.jsonc`. Your `provider.amazon-bedrock` + `enabled_providers: ["amazon-bedrock"]` is project-scoped config that only the per-directory fetch would pick up, and that's exactly the call that gets swallowed. So global is empty, the fallback is empty, and the picker is empty. This matches your debug log showing HTTP hits to `provider` but no `service=provider` lines — the per-directory `provider.list()` is short-circuited inside the app before the server's provider init runs.

(Note: the same bug is also why everyone sees an empty model picker for a few seconds at startup before the global list arrives — that's a milder version of the same issue, not a separate problem.)

### Fix

Swap the key to `loadProvidersQuery(input.directory)`. PR up at #23134.

cc @Brendonovich (author of #22756) — looks like a copy-paste from the sessions block.

The below comment is the summarization related to further long investigation

---

**Further investigation notes**

The fix is correct beyond the stated model-switch scenario.
**`differentModel` can be spuriously `true` without switching models.**

`prompt.ts:1415` stores messages with \`model.id\` (e.g. \`global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6\`).
`provider.ts:1333` sets `model.api.id = model.api.id ?? model.id ?? modelID` — these can diverge.
`message-v2.ts:692` compares `model.providerID/model.id` vs `msg.info.providerID/msg.info.modelID`.

If anything along that chain resolves differently between turns, `differentModel` flips `true` on the same model.

**`compaction.ts:218` is the likely trigger at large context.**

When context approaches the model limit, auto-compaction calls `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect` to reconstruct the full history. If `differentModel` is `true` at that point, every accumulated thinking block across all turns loses its signature simultaneously — which is why the error surfaces near the context limit rather than on the turn that first stripped a signature.

**Regardless of the trigger, the fix is the right one.**

For text/tool parts, stripping provider metadata on model change is correct — prevents e.g. OpenAI `itemId` leaking to Anthropic.
For reasoning parts it is never correct — Anthropic embeds a cryptographic signature in `providerMetadata` that it verifies on every subsequent turn. Once stripped it cannot be reconstructed.

The affected line: `message-v2.ts:794`
```ts
// before
...(differentModel ? {} : { providerMetadata: part.metadata }),
// after
providerMetadata: part.metadata,
```

Refers to #1439
